title: Efficient Coagulant Production from Moringa Oleifera Seeds for Water Treatment
author: Hounsinou, Assogba, et al.
materials: of stock coagulant solution and/or a volume (V

steps.title: Harvest and shell seeds
steps.instruction: Collect mature Moringa oleifera seeds, remove their shells, and keep the seed kernels for further processing.

steps.title: Crush seed kernels
steps.instruction: Grind the shelled seed kernels into a fine powder using a crusher or mortar.

steps.title: Extract oil from powder
steps.instruction: Subject the Moringa oleifera powder to an oil‑extraction method (e.g., solvent extraction) to separate the oil fraction.

steps.title: Extract salts from powder
steps.instruction: Dissolve the remaining Moringa oleifera cake in a saline solution to obtain the coagulant salts.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.5 L of 1 mol L⁻¹ aqueous NaCl solution to a beaker.
Add 2.5 g of the Moringa oleifera cake to the NaCl solution.
Stir the mixture with a magnetic stirrer for 30 min.
Filter the suspension through filter paper; retain the filtrate for later use.

steps.title: Microfilter the extract
steps.instruction: Pass the filtrate obtained from the salt‑extraction step through a 0.2 µm membrane filter to remove fine particulates.

steps.title: Lyophilize to dry coagulant
steps.instruction: Freeze‑dry (lyophilize) the micro‑filtered solution to obtain the final coagulant in dry form.

steps.title: Set up jar‑test beakers
steps.instruction: Prepare six beakers in the jar‑test device, each containing 0.5 L of lake water of known turbidity.

steps.title: Prepare stock coagulant solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 100 mg of the dry Moringa coagulant in 100 mL of distilled water to make a 1 mg mL⁻¹ stock solution.

steps.title: Make 1/10 dilution
steps.instruction: Transfer 10 mL of the stock solution to a clean container and add 90 mL of distilled water, yielding a 1/10 dilution.

steps.title: Make 1/100 dilution
steps.instruction: Transfer 10 mL of the 1/10 dilution to another container and add 90 mL of distilled water, yielding a 1/100 dilution.

steps.title: Dose beakers with coagulant
steps.instruction: Using a graduated pipette, add appropriate volumes of stock, 1/10, and/or 1/100 solutions to beakers 2–6 to achieve the desired coagulant dose; leave beaker 1 as the untreated control.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the dose D (mg L⁻¹) with D = (m ÷ V) (2 V₁ + V₂ ÷ 5 + V₃ ÷ 50), where V, V₁, V₂, V₃ are in mL and m is the mass of coagulant (mg).
Add the calculated volumes V₁ (stock), V₂ (1/10 dilution), and V₃ (1/100 dilution) to each beaker.

steps.title: Stir and rest mixtures
steps.instruction: Stir each beaker’s water‑coagulant mixture for 30 min, then allow the suspensions to stand undisturbed for 1 hour before measuring turbidity.
